QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_24

question.text: Which tool is most appropriate for calculating returns on systematic investment plans (SIPs) with multiple irregular cash flows?

explanation.text: The Logic: XIRR is used for investments with multiple cash inflows and outflows along with their corresponding dates, which is exactly the structure of a periodic mutual fund investment such as a SIP. The workbook illustrates this with quarterly Rs.10,000 investments yielding about 14.26% XIRR. The Trap: CAGR, simple annualized return and absolute return all assume a single inflow or a single growth-from-start-to-end value, so they cannot correctly handle multiple periodic investments at different dates. Note: The defining feature of XIRR is that it takes both cash-flow amounts and the dates on which they occur.
